newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-JAMAICA FINED AND WARNED FOLLOWING BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JAMAICA FINED AND WARNED FOLLOWING BRAWL.

text.p: The Jamaican Football Association were fined 50,000 Swiss francs ($34,000) and warned they could face expulsion from the World Cup following a brawl with a Mexican team in a friendly on March 31.

FIFA, world soccer's governing body, also fined the Mexican Football Association 25,000 Swiss francs ($17,000) and the Toros Neza club 10,000 Swiss francs ($7,000) for the incidents which forced the match to be abandoned.
The match was part of Jamaica's preparations for their World Cup qualifier against Mexico on April 13 which Mexico subsequently won 6-0.
FIFA warned the Jamaicans that if any similar incidents occurred, they would be punished more severely and could even be kicked out of the World Cup qualifiers.
Jamaica are currently struggling in fifth place in the six-team final CONCACAF group competition, having drawn two and lost one of their three matches.
Several Mexican players were injured when members of both squads punched and kicked each other for several minutes during the match.
Several Jamaican players then stormed off the field and returned waving bricks and broken glass to hold the angry Mexican side at bay.

Jamaica were leading Toros Neza 1-0 in the 19th minute when a Jamaican midfielder slid into Toros's Argentine-born German Arangio. He got to his feet and punched the Jamaican tackler and an all-out fight ensued.
